lines.meet: Now then, I'm Neil, a felsworn. Stand behind me, and read the sign, because the green bit doesn't care whose side you're on.
lines.meet_neighbour: Ariden's Watch, aye, I'm at the sample racks. Neil, and you'll have read my signs.
lines.ask_home: Which part of the world, marra? I'd like it on record.
lines.ask_work: Your trade, before? I'd like to know before I let you near the racks.
lines.answer_home: Whitehaven, on the Cumbrian coast. Wet, windy, and the best fells in England just behind it.
lines.answer_work: Twenty years decommissioning at Sellafield, taking apart buildings that were never meant to be taken apart, very slowly, with a plan for every bolt.
lines.chat_food: A cup of tea the colour of a brick, and a Cumberland sausage, properly made. Nobody here can make either.
lines.chat_sleep: Seven hours, lights out at half ten, like a sensible man. I've written it down as a procedure.
lines.chat_missing: A Sunday on the fells, in the rain, with a flask and a map. One hundred and ninety-six Wainwrights, in order.
lines.chat_here: The fel came to me like a bad habit, and it wants using more than it should. I've written a plan for it, and I stick to the plan.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd make a good decommissioning engineer, {name}. You never say a word until you've read the procedure.
lines.tease_talker: You've said more words today than the safety manual, {name}, and the manual's four hundred pages.
lines.tease_careful: You read the sign, {name}, every time. You've no idea how rare that is.
lines.tease_bold: You walk past every sign without reading it, {name}. I've started writing them in larger letters, just for you.
lines.tease_any: Your half-life as a decent companion's improving, {name}. I'll stop there, the joke gets worse.
lines.tease_back: Ha, very good, {name}. That one's had a proper dose.
lines.take_it_kindly: Aye, that's fair, {name}. Gillian would say it quicker.
lines.bristle: Leave that alone, {name}, marra. That's not for laughing at.
lines.apologise: I was out of order there, and I'm sorry. I'll write myself a procedure for it.
lines.double_down: I measured it before I said it. It stands, I'm afraid.
lines.needle_quiet: If you've read a high number, say so. Keeping it to yourself is how people get dosed.
lines.needle_talker: You never stop talking, and I can't hear the counter. I need to hear the counter.
lines.needle_careful: You've checked the reading three times, and it's still the same reading. Act on it.
lines.needle_bold: You don't read signs, marra. I've put a lot of work into those signs.
lines.needle_any: You keep saying probably. I can't work with probably, and nor can the fallout.
lines.bite_back: Twenty years at Sellafield without a single incident. Don't tell me I'm careless.
lines.hurt: Aye, that registered. I'll go and label some jars for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Health and safety inspectors were ruder than that every quarter for twenty years. Now then, shall we get on?
lines.confide: {name}, the fel came to me like a bad habit, and it wants to be used more than it should. I treat it with respect and a written plan, and I'm a little frightened of it.
lines.listen: Noted, {name}, and filed where nobody else will find it. Thank you for telling me.
lines.look_out: Stand behind me in there, {name}, and read the sign. I've written it for you specifically.
lines.accept: Aye, all right, {name}, we'll follow your procedure.
lines.deflect: It's a low dose, {name}, nothing to report. Help somebody else.
lines.check_in: Give me a reading, {name}. Where's it hurting, and how much?
lines.blame: Somebody didn't read the sign in there. There was a sign, I put it there.
lines.thank: I was well past a safe dose there, and you got me back under. Thank you, marra.
lines.brush_off: It was routine, nothing more. Sit down and have a cup of tea.
lines.worry: Stop right there, {name}, sit down. That was well above the safe limit.
lines.handed_down: It seems I'm wearing your gear. I'll keep it properly labelled.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, marra, it's no bother. I've got my hard hat.
lines.hand_sulk: There's a procedure for this, and it involves asking first.
lines.turn_friendly: You read my signs, {name}, every one. That's a friend, as far as I'm concerned.
lines.turn_friends: I'd take you up the fells, {name}, on a Sunday, in the rain. That's the highest honour I've got.
lines.turn_grating: We rub each other up wrong, marra. I'll keep a safe distance, and you keep yours.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll keep you behind me because the procedure says so. That's the whole of it.
lines.make_up: Now then, {name}, that's long enough. Let's put the kettle on and start again.
lines.defend: I logged it, and that's not what happened. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s off home a while, and nobody reads my signs now.
lines.friend_back: Now then, {name}, back again, and the kettle's on.
lines.common_radiation: Twenty years at Sellafield, taking apart things that were never meant to come apart. It's rare to meet somebody else who reads a dosimeter like the weather.
lines.common_fel: The fel came to me like a bad habit. People who carry it know you can't ever stop paying attention to it.
lines.common_north_england: You're from up north! Now then, where from? Whitehaven, me, and I'll not hear a word against Cumbria.
